newsitem.title: UK: LME copper unmoved by Sumitomo loss announcement.
newsitem.headline: LME copper unmoved by Sumitomo loss announcement.

text.p: London Metal Exchange prices and traders were little moved early on Thursday by Sumitomo Corp's admission that its copper trading losses were greater than first thought.

Sumitomo admitted that losses from the massive copper trading scandal which rocked the world's metal markets earlier this year were $2.6 billion, not the $1.8 billion estimated when the news of losses first emerged.
"The size of the loss is really Sumitomo's problem, not the market's," one analyst said.
The statement came as part of a revision of the trading group's earnings forecast.
The companmy also stated that it would sue its former chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka over massive copper losses.

Sumitomo president Kenji Miyahara told a news conference on Thursday the company had liquidated most of its open, uncovered copper positions, although it still has some long and short positions in the market.
"Accordingly, there is almost no risk remaining and it is our judgment that we will not again revise the estimated loss we have announced today," he added.
An LME dealer said, "We knew that they had cleared out most of their positions so I don't see this having an impact.
"The market is little changed this morning. We're expecting to see a continuation of yesterday's short-covering rally," he added.
One analyst was fairly dimsissive of Sumitomo's comment this morning that all its losses came through its LME activities.
"I don't think that's new. It did business on the LME and Comex and also in physical. We always assumed there were losses on the LME," he said.
At 0740 GMT, the three months copper position on the LME was indicated at $1,944/$1,948 a tonne compared with an after-hours close of $1,925 on Wednesday.
